task.title: Resetting superuser passwords on Red Hat Quay standalone deployments
task.shortdesc: To reset the superuser password on your Red Hat Quay standalone deployment, you can generate a bcrypt-hashed password with Python, exec into the PostgreSQL container with podman exec, and update the user table with the new hashed password.

ul.li: You have created a Red Hat Quay superuser.
You have installed the pip package manager for Python.
You have installed the bcrypt package for pip.

step.cmd: Generate a secure, hashed password using the bcrypt package in Python 3.9 by entering the following command:
Enter the following command to show the container ID of your Red Hat Quay container registry:

info.codeblock: CONTAINER ID IMAGE COMMAND CREATED STATUS PORTS NAMES 70560beda7aa registry.redhat.io/rhel8/redis-5:1 run-redis 2 hours ago Up 2 hours ago 0.0.0.0:6379->6379/tcp redis 8012f4491d10 registry.redhat.io/quay/quay-rhel8:v3.8.2 registry 3 minutes ago Up 8 seconds ago 0.0.0.0:80->8080/tcp, 0.0.0.0:443->8443/tcp quay 8b35b493ac05 registry.redhat.io/rhel8/postgresql-10:1 run-postgresql 39 seconds ago Up 39 seconds ago 0.0.0.0:5432->5432/tcp postgresql-quay

step.cmd: Execute an interactive shell for the postgresql container image by entering the following command:
Re-enter the quay PostgreSQL database server, specifying the database, username, and host address:
Update the password_hash of the superuser admin who lost their password:

info.codeblock: quay=> UPDATE public.user SET password_hash = '$2b$12$T8pkgtOoys3G5ut7FV1She6vXlYgU.6TeoGmbbAVQtN8X8ch4knKm' where username = 'quayadmin';

step.cmd: Enter the following to command to ensure that the password_hash has been updated:
Log in to your Red Hat Quay deployment using the new password:

info.codeblock: $ sudo podman login -u quayadmin -p newpass1234 http://quay-server.example.com --tls-verify=false
